Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh's bowling wasn't at its best early in the Australian innings. However, they managed to improve their performance yesterday. Mustafizur Rahman finished with a 4-fer and was the most successful bowler as the Bangla spinners struggled for consistency. Now, the hosts will have to bat really well to first erase the deficit and then build on a lead. Stay tuned, they will be out soon.

Australia will be pleased with their batting but at the same time will know that they could have done even better. David Warner, Steven Smith and Peter Handscomb played exceedingly well to set the tempo but the lower middle order didn't contribute much. The likes of Glenn Maxwell and Matthew Wade went into a shell when they should have dominated after tea yesterday and that probably has cost them a few runs.

So, it took Bangladesh 11 balls today to pick the last wicket as Australia failed to add even a single run to their overnight lead. Anyway, the lead which the tourists have gained is still a handy one with the pitch deteriorating every minute.

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage for the fourth day of the 2nd Test between Bangladesh and Australia. The visitors have batted decently and now they will want their last pair to pile up as many runs as possible. Bangladesh, on the other hand, will look to start batting as soon as possible, as they are already 72 runs behind in the game. With rain clouds still looming, we hope that we get a full day of cricket. It's bright and sunny as of now. The first ball isn't faraway.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

The last pair of Steve O'Keefe and Nathan Lyon is out in the middle and the visitors will be content with whatever these two add tomorrow. The hosts on the other hand have to get the final wicket first and then get over the deficit to set a target for the Aussies. We have an early start on day 4 to make up for the lost overs today. The action begins at 0930 local (0330 GMT). See you then! Take care! Cheers!

Bangladesh's bowlers were much better in the last session. Mustafizur Rahman mixed up lines and lengths nicely while Mehedi Hasan got rewards for his probing lines. Their fielding though was very ordinary. They would be ruing their lost chances as Australia kept stretching their lead, which is 72 currently.

Ashton Agar then tried to provide some resistance with Pat Cummins but both didn't last long.

Glenn Maxwell holds the key from here on for the Aussies. They lead by 16 runs currently and will be aiming for at least 100 runs with five wickets in hand. The hosts will have to bowl a lot better and take their catches if they don't want to play the catching game. Do join us in a short while.

A good session of Test cricket. 96/3 in the 31 overs bowled. The play in the morning was completely washed out. Once it started after the lunch break, the Australian pair of Handscomb and Warner looked in fine touch again. However, the run out of the former gave the hosts a sniff. David Warner went on to score his century and along with Glenn Maxwell was building a good partnership when Mustafizur Rahman removed him. A brief resistance was provided by Hilton Cartwright but he played a poor shot to gift his wicket away just before the tea break.

Maxwell defends it back to the bowler with a straight bat.
The man now moves to deep cover. Reactive captaincy from Rahim!
Wide outside off, spinning away. Sits nicely for Maxwell, who goes back and cracks it powerfully towards covers. Tamim there, makes an awkward stop. Shakib gets away with this one.
Fired around off, Maxwell blocks it neatly.
Second new ball is taken straightaway! Shakib Al Hasan will continue with it.
Pitched outside off, Warner covers his stumps and blocks it on the off side.
Fuller on the stumps, driven back to the bowler.
Spinning into the batsman, Maxwell prods forward and nudges it off the inner half behind square on the leg side. A single is taken.
Quicker through the air outside off, spinning in, Maxwell leans ahead and defends it down the track.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full around off, spinning in, pushed back to the bowler.
Full outside off, eased through mid off for a single.
Glenn Maxwell once again gets on the top of the ball and blocks it.
Sliding into the batsman, Maxwell presents another solid front foot defence.
Maxwell plants his front foot to the pitch of the ball and blocks it on the up.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full outside off, driven through covers for a single.
A touch shorter, punched through cover-point for a single.
Warner hangs back and defends.

FOUR! There it is! The moment Warner was waiting for! 20th Test ton for him, his third one in Asia. Hossain slants it across but ends up bowling a low full toss. Warner caresses it superbly through covers and the ball races away to the fence. He celebrates in his typical manner, kissing the badge on his cap and then jumping and pumping his arms in the air. What a knock it has been! Absolutely superb! Centuries in consecutive innings for him. Although, this is his slowest ton, it will be the most satisfying one.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Change of gloves for David Warner!

Quicker through the air around leg, Warner pushes it down the track on the leg side and takes off for a single. But immediately turns back, seeing Hossain get to the ball. Nasir moves to his left, picks up the ball and fires a throw at the other end but misses. However, Warner had made it in with a full-stretched dive. He needs to be patient, the run will eventually come.
Fuller around off, Warner presses forward and pushes it to covers.
Floated outside off, Maxwell goes for a big shot again. Mistimes it and is lucky that the ball falls wide of the fielder at mid off. Two runs taken in the process.
Quicker outside off, Maxwell fails to cut it through.
Outside off, played towards short third man off the outside edge.
FOUR! Floats this one around off, Maxwell gets under the ball and manages to hit it over the bowler's head for a boundary. Not a clean hit but still manages to get the runs which matter.
Shorter around middle and leg, Maxwell stays in his crease and punches it back to the bowler.
Sprayed down the leg side, Maxwell goes back and pushes it towards mid on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. Three consecutive maidens!
Slants it across the southpaw, Warner shuffles across and lets it pass to the keeper.
Fuller on middle and leg, Warner turns it to mid on.
Blocked towards mid off, off the front foot.
Warner strides ahead and pushes it towards mid off.
Quicker one on the pads, turned to backward square leg.
Fuller outside off, driven towards covers.
Maxwell camps back and blocks it away.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Maxwell tries to defend it, gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Floated around off, Maxwell gets forward and defends it.
Maxwell camps back and defends it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Warner clips it on the leg side.
Warner gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.

OUT! What a way to get a breakthrough! Just when Australia looked to be cruising, a stunning throw from Shakib has halted their journey! Shorter and spinning into the batsman, Warner camps back and clips it towards mid-wicket. Handscomb calls for the single and goes rushing for it. Warner sends him back immediately but Handscomb is a bit late in turning back. Shakib rushes towards the ball and scores a direct hit at the non-striker's end. The umpire goes upstairs and Bangladesh are confident. Replays show that even the dive from Peter Handscomb couldn't save him. A brilliant knock comes to a tragic end. Glenn Maxwell strides in with Australia trailing by 55 runs.
Wait, this is the last thing Australia wanted! The umpire has gone upstairs to check for a run out appeal against Handscomb! Bangladesh seem pretty confident!
Warner stays in his crease and defends it neatly.
Gives it air this time and pitches this one around leg, Warner gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.
Nasir Hossain is brought in for a bowl.
Fuller outside off, Handscomb leans forward and blocks it away.
Floated around off, PH gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
Around middle and leg, Peter flicks it but fails to beat the diving fielder at mid-wicket.
Shorter and angling into the pads, Handscomb comes forward and nudges it towards mid-wicket.
Driven through covers for a single.
Flatter outside off, the ball stays low. Actually very, very low. Warner was totally beaten as he tried to push it on the off side.
Floated outside off, Warner pushes it towards covers for a quick single. Just two runs short of another hundred!
Warner stays in his crease and clips it on the leg side.
Tossed up around off, Handscomb drives it towards wide mid off and rushes for a single. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but he misses. Also brings up the 150-run stand between the two.
Floated outside off, Warner leans forward and drives. The extra cover fielder dives to his left and saves a certain boundary. A run is taken.
Warner lunges forward only to make a block.
Around off, Warner stays deep in his crease and defends it towards point.
Around middle and leg, nudged towards the fielder at short mid-wicket.
Floated outside off, PH gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Handscomb gets forward to block it away.
Peter stays in his crease and punches it towards mid on.
Floated around off, Handscomb lunges forward and defends it.
Drifting into the pads, clipped towards fine leg for a single.
Fuller into the pads, clipped straight to the fielder at mid-wicket. An inch here and there and the ball would have raced away to the fence.
Fuller into the stumps, Handscomb leans forward and defends it.
Around middle and off, Handscomb clips it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Quicker outside off, Warner gets his bat down to push it through the off side for a single.
Shorter around off, Handscomb hangs back a touch and punches it elegantly through the cover-point region for a triple.
Sprayed a bit short around off, Warner works it towards deep mid-wicket for an easy single.
Shorter outside off, Handscomb goes for the punch. Mistimes it back down the wicket.
Handscomb gets on his front foot to defend the fuller delivery outside off.
Tossed up around middle and off, Peter gets behind the ball to defend it.
Handscomb lunges forward and defends it.
Floats this one around off, Handscomb reaches the pitch of the ball and blocks it away.
Sprayed down the leg side, pulled through the backward square leg region for a single.
Handscomb stays deep in his crease and defends it.
Handscomb gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
FOUR! Freebies! Sprayed down the leg side, Handscomb has all the time in the world to adjust and pull it through the backward square leg region for a boundary.
Played towards mid-wicket.
Flatter outside off, Handscomb stays deep in his crease and defends it.
Spinning in from around off, Handscomb gets forward to defend. Ends up hitting it towards square leg off the inner half.
Tossed up outside off, Warner reaches to the pitch of the ball and clips it towards mid on.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Again a delivery on a shorter length, Warner camps back and punches it through the cover-point region for a couple.
Floated outside off, David gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.
Around off, clipped towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Warner stays deep in his crease and guides it towards short third man.
Quicker around middle and leg, Peter gets his bat down in time to defend it neatly.
Spinning away from around off, Warner stays deep in his crease and flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Mehedi bowls this really short this time, Handscomb charges a touch, adjusts himself and just clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up around off, Peter leans forward and pushes it through the backward point region for a couple. This also helps him bring his highest Test score away from home.
Around middle and leg, Handscomb also gets his first runs of the day as he clips it through the mid-wicket region for a couple.
Floats this one around off, Handscomb prods forward and defends it.
Mehedi Hasan to start from the other end.
Leg bye! Sprayed down the leg side, Handscomb fails to clip it through. Goes off his pads, past the keeper for a leg bye.
Floats it around middle and leg, Warner dances down the track and clips it through the mid-wicket region for a single.
Short outside off, spinning in. Warner stays in his crease and defends it on the off side.
Again angling into the pads, Warner gets a bit forward and pushes it towards mid on.
Fuller into the pads, driven towards mid on.
Shorter outside off, the ball stays low. Warner tries to cut but gets beaten by the lack of bounce. Bangladesh will like that.
The players are out in the middle. Shakib Al Hasan to start the proceedings with the ball for Bangladesh. David Warner to face him first up. A slip and a short leg in place. Here we go...
Right, then! Our long wait has finally come to an end. Play will begin at 1315 local time. A minimum of 67 overs to be bowled today.

Update 1252 local time - Steve O'Keefe and Brendon Julian are in conversation near the pitch. They are pointing towards a particular area, mainly the zone outside off for the left-handers. The Australian coach, Darren Lehmann was also out there inspecting the surface a little while back. Meanwhile, the groundsmen are at work. If no more rain, we will be getting underway soon. Stay with us...

Update 1230 local time - We've some good news for you! The rain has stopped and the covers are slowly coming off. Good part is that the sun has come out as well which will help the groundsmen. The match officials are also on the ground inspecting the conditions. Let's hope for a prompt start after the lunch break.
Update 1200 local time - The rain is still pouring down. The covers remain in place. Meanwhile, lunch has been taken. Let's hope for some good news after the break. Do join us in a short while.

Update 1045 local time - The conditions have not improved much and the covers are still on. The rain continues to come down and it seems unlikely that we will have any play in the first session. Let's be positive. Stay tuned, we will keep you posted...
Update 0945 local time - Unfortunately, the last thing we least wanted has arrived. Yes, it's raining and is quite heavy at the moment. Hope it eases off and we get some play soon.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, will look to keep their heads high and they would back themselves to run through the Australian side as quickly as possible. Shakib Al Hasan will look to recreate his magic and try to push the Kangaroos on the back foot. The first session of the day will be vital as it could very well push the game in one team's favour. An exciting day of cricket awaits. Stay tuned.

Hello and a warm welcome to the coverage of the third day of the 2nd Test between Bangladesh and Australia in Chittagong. The visitors are in a respectable position thanks to an unbeaten 127-run stand between Handscomb and Warner. Their presence in the middle could well prove to be the difference between the sides. The tourists would hope they keep on piling up runs and gain a big lead.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

The hosts on the other hand were wayward with their bowling. They looked clueless and lacked ideas. Also, some missed opportunities and poor tactics from their skipper have put them on the back foot. A good night's rest is what they need and they would want to come fresh tomorrow in the hope of inflicting a collapse. There is turn and uneven bounce on offer but it is not that threatening. We are in for an eventful day of cricket. Do join us for all the action from day 3 at 1000 local (0400 GMT). Till then, take care and cheers!

A wicketless session for Bangladesh has turned the match in Australia's favour. An unbeaten 126-run stand between Handscomb and Warner has seen the visitors cut the deficit down to 80. The former fought his way through and is unbeaten on 69 whereas the latter had his share of luck and is 12 runs short of what would be a brilliant hundred. The away side have momentum on their side and they will now try and bat the home side out of the game.
Arm ball wide outside off, Handscomb plants his front foot across and shoulders his arms. He survives the over and the day. He will now resume with Warner tomorrow as IT'S STUMPS ON DAY 2!
Full outside off, Peter takes a big stride forward and blocks it neatly.
Tossed up around off, spinning away, Handscomb dances down the track. Doesn't get to the ball but still manages to defend it down the track.
Landed full outside off, tapped past silly point towards extra cover.
Full around off, Handscomb leans ahead and blocks it towards silly point.
Tossed up outside off, spinning in, Warner dances down and drives it through wide mid on for a single.
Floats it on middle, Handscomb defends it towards mid-wicket.
Darts it on off, David punches it through covers for a run.
Shorter in length on off, Warner pushes it to covers.
Fires it on the pads, Peter flicks it down to fine leg for a run.
Flatter on off, Peter defends it watchfully.
Tosses it up on off, Handscomb defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Sees the flighted delivery and advances down the track to flick it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Uses his feet, gets down to the pitch of the ball and eases it towards wide mid off.
Slower through the air on off, PH defends it solidly.
Tosses it up on off, Peter defends it off the front foot.
Quicker on off, Handscomb drives it back to the bowler.
Fuller on off, Warner drives it back to the bowler.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Tosses it up on off, Warner defends it off the front foot.
Full toss on off, Peter flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Fires it full on the pads, Warner flicks it with the angle through wide mid on for a run.
Flatter ball on off, Handscomb comes down the track, drives it towards mid off and sets off for a run. The fielder there has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. A run added to the total.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Quicker on off, David cuts it to covers.
Comes down the track and drives it through covers for a run.
This time to Nasir's right! Drags his length back outside off, Warner cuts it towards deep point for a run.
Floats it on off, Warner defends it off the front foot.
A poor ball to start off. Short and wide outside off. Warner camps back and cuts it through cover-point. Nasir Hossain in the deep runs to his left and keeps it down to two.
Taijul Islam is back into the attack.
Tosses it up on off, Handscomb does well to defend it.
Flatter on middle, Warner tries to defend but gets it off the inner half through square leg for a run.

Peter Handscomb might be feeling the heat here. He is struggling at the moment. The physio is out and Handscomb has an ice pack on his head and is being wiped by the wet towel. He is also having a energy drink so that he does not get dehydrated.
Slower through the air on middle, turning into the batsman. Handscomb tries to defend but gets it off the inner half towards square leg for a run.
Plays the paddle sweep to the ball on leg stump fine down the leg side for a couple.
Flatter on off, no turn in offer. Peter defends it watchfully.
Tosses it up on middle. Handscomb defends it off the front foot.
This is getting too easy for the Australians. Rahman bowls it short and outside off. Warner cuts it through point for two.
Very short on middle, Warner pulls it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Serves a full toss on off, Warner drives it through covers for a boundary.
Shorter in length outside off, Warner cuts it through point for a couple.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short ball on the pads, Handscomb mistimes his pull towards short fine leg for a run. It was a poor delivery, deserved to be hit for a boundary.
Sabbir Rahman is into the attack now.
Drags his length back outside off. Warner plays it to point.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Flatter on off, Warner defends it off the front foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
BEATEN! Ahhh! This wicket is starting to talk now. Hasan bowls it slower through the air on off, turning away. Warner tries to defend it but gets beaten.

Another reprieve for Warner! Mushfiqur Rahim misses a stumping. Mehedi bowls it slower through the air outside off. Warner comes down the track and goes for a heave but is beaten by the lack of bounce which also foxes the keeper. The ball hits Rahim low on the pads and rolls past the stumps. A big, big miss there. The dropped chance earlier and now Bangladesh have given him another chance. How costly will this prove? Warner also needs to be more wise and not get carried away like he did here, stepping out straightaway against Mehedi in his new spell.
Mehedi Hasan is back into the attack.
Off pace delivery on leg stump. Handscomb with a lot of ease plays it towards mid-wicket.
Fuller on the pads, Handscomb flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Very full delivery outside off. Peter jams it out to mid off.
Very full and wide outside off. The batsman lets it be.
Slower ball on middle, Handscomb defends it with ease.
Shorter in length outside off, Warner cuts it through point for a run.
Fuller on middle. Peter flicks it on the leg side.
Floats it on off, turning back in. Warner works it towards square leg for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Warner defends it watchfully.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drags his length back on off, Handscomb punches it down to long off for a run.
100-run stand between Peter Handscomb and David Warner.
Works it with the spin towards square leg for a run.
Too easy for the Australian batsmen. Fuller outside off, Peter drives it through covers, does not quite time it. The batsmen take two.
Good length on middle. Peter shuffles across and defends it.
FOUR! A gift but it still has to be put away! A full toss outside off. Handscomb just guides it through backward point for a boundary.
Very full on off, trying to get him LBW. Handscomb is up for the challenge and keeps it out easily.
Back of a length on leg stump. Peter tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Lands it on a length around off, angling across the batsman. Handscomb stays inside the crease and defends it.
Fires it on the pads, Warner fails to flick it and the ball brushes the pads and goes to short fine leg.
Tosses it up on off, David defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Shorter in length on off, turning away. Peter punches it through the off side for a run.
Drags his length back outside off, turns back in. Warner pushes it down to long off for a run.
Flatter on the stumps, angling into the batsman. Peter flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Mominul Haque comes into the attack.
Fuller on middle, Warner shuffles across and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Lands it on a length on middle, Warner works it towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller on the pads. Peter works it around the corner for a run.
Angles it into the batsman. Warner flicks it through square leg for a run.
4th Test fifty for Peter Handscomb.

Fifty for Handscomb! He will look to covert this into a big one and not throw it away. Rahman lands it on a length around off, Handscomb guides it towards the slip cordon. The fielder at second slip dives to his right and makes a half stop. The batsmen run through for a single.
Shorter in length outside off, Peter punches it through covers for a run.
Handscomb runs down the track. Islam drags his length back. Peter adjusts and defends it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Advances down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.

FOUR! JUST OVER! Brilliant anticipation by Sarkar but to no avail! Islam fires it on the stumps. Handscomb goes for the sweep but gets a top edge. Sarkar at first slip sees him going down for the shot and runs towards his left but the ball goes just over him and races to the fence.
Tosses it up on off, Handscomb defends it off the front foot.
A cutter on middle, Warner defends it towards square leg.
Full and on the pads, Peter flicks it through square leg for a run.

FOUR! SLAPPED! Poor ball. Even with six fielders on the off side Handscomb hits it for a boundary. Rahman bowls it short and outside off, sits up to be hit. Peter slashes it over cover and into the fence.
Back of a length on off, Handscomb rocks back and defends it.
Angles it into the pads of the batsman. He flicks it to mid-wicket.
Full and wide outside off, a loosener you can say. Peter lets it be.
Time for pace! Mustafizur Rahman comes into the attack.

Drinks. Australia are cruising at the moment. These two have continued to pile on the runs and they only trail by another 132. The hosts on the other hand, will need someone to put their hand up and produce some magic.
Bowls it in the flatter trajectory, on middle and on the shorter side, Peter moves back and punches it through covers for a single.
Flatter and shorter on off, hit across the line in front of square leg for a run.
Drifts into the batsman and lands around off, spinning away, Handscomb gets back inside the crease and plays it with the spin towards point. A single taken.
Too full in length, around middle, Warner skips down and punches it past the short mid on fielder for a single.
Spinning back into the batsman from around off, Warner leans forward and defends it from the inside half of the bat.
Full and around off, Handscomb drives it after coming down the track towards long off for one.
Nasir Hossain has been seen warming up. He might come into bowl. We shall wait and see.

Loopy and on middle, Handscomb skips down the track and works it through mid-wicket for a single. The throw comes to the bowler's end and Mehedi deflects it onto the stumps. He appeals repeatedly but the umpire fails to entertain him. At last, the bowler smiles and takes his cap.
Fuller and on off, driven past the diving short cover fielder for a single.
A miscued shot! Lovely delivery, an off spinner landing on off, Warner tries flicking but closes the face of the bat early. It takes the leading edge and rolls safely towards backward point.
Quicker one, a shade on the shorter side outside off, Peter adjusts well and taps it down wide of backward point for a run.
Extra flight this time, full and on off, Warner advances down the track and hits it firmly through widish mid on for a single.
Starts this new spell from around the wicket for the right-hander. Serves a flighted ball on middle and it's worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Mehedi Hasan is back on.
Use of the feet by Peter as he caresses his drive through mid off for a single.
Flatter and around middle, Handscomb is stuck inside the crease and defends it at the last moment off his back leg. Dead plumb had he missed.
Fuller and on middle, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Very full and on off, Warner nearly falls across as he pushes it back to the bowler.
Slower this time, full and outside off, turning back in, Warner gets forward and defends it back.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished. Short and wide outside off, Warner camps back and smacks it through covers for a boundary. Hit ferociously.

FOUR! That's put away exceedingly well. Shakib bowls it slower through the air and gives it extra flight. Handscomb uses his feet to run down to the pitch of the ball and flicks it aerially over mid-wicket for a boundary. He has been very swift with his footwork.
Full and around leg, Warner eases it down through mid on for a single.
Quicker this time, full and on the pads, Warner keeps it out to backward square leg.
Slower through the air, full and around leg, Warner flicks it from his pads to backward square leg.
Bunts a full ball down to mid off for a quick single.

Flights it up in the air and Handscomb's initial movement was to get down the track. But he then picks the length which is on the shorter side and hence cuts it from the back foot through backward point. A couple taken.
Walks down the track and pushes it down to long off for one.

Not out! The third umpire spots an inside edge. Taijul serves an arm ball around off, skidding back in as Handscomb skips down the track and tries to defend with his bat and pad together. He misses and they appeal vociferously. Nothing from the umpire and Rahim opts for the DRS. The Hawk Eye shows that it's pretty adjacent to the wickets but the Ultra Edge reflects that there is a little bit of inside edge. Handscomb survives!
Huge shout for an lbw! Not given. Mushfiqur Rahim takes the referral.
Slower and fuller around off, Handscomb rather than getting forward decides to defend it from the back foot. Risky!
Once again uses his feet but this time drives a full ball straight back to the bowler.
Tosses it up in the air and lands it full around leg, Handscomb gets forward and defends it from the inner half of the bat.
Jumps down the track and flicks a full ball to short mid-wicket. A diving stop by the fielder.
Slower and fuller around leg, Warner fails to work it off his pads.
50-run stand between Peter Handscomb and David Warner.

Not out! Well and truly in. A tossed up ball on off, Handscomb hurries down the track and drives it to mid off. It's going straight towards the fielder and he takes the challenge of stealing a single. A direct throw at the non-striker's end but Handscomb is found safe in the replays.
Appeal for a run out is referred upstairs.
Goes slower through the air and bowls it with a round-arm action. It drops on a fuller length around off and Handscomb prods forward in defense.
Full and on middle, worked in front of square leg for a single.
Arm ball around off, skidding through the surface, Warner pushes inside the line and misses.
Quicker ball on off, Warner defends it off his back foot.
Taijul gives it extra air and lands it full on off, Warner advances down the track and forces it to long on for one.
Sharp spin back into the batsman from a shorter length outside off, Warner defends it from the crease with an angled bat.
Uses his feet and works it towards wide mid on for one.
Almost hits the yorker length this time, on middle, Peter digs it out at the last moment.
Slower through the air, drifting in around off, Handscomb presses forward in defense.
Floated delivery, too full outside off, Warner drives it in front of square on the off side for a single.
Bowls it quicker through the air and lands it full on off, Handscomb drives it off his front foot to short cover.
Shakib hurls across an arm ball on middle, Peter goes deep inside the crease and keeps it out from the inner half of the bat to mid-wicket.
Gives this one some extra loop and lands it very full on off, Warner walks forward and pushes it back to Shakib.
Full flighted around leg, Warner nudges it off his pads to backward square leg.
Flatter delivery, a touch short and around off, David packs a punch from the crease but finds the extra cover fielder.
Spinning down the leg side, it's worked off the pads to backward square leg.
Arm ball on off, skidding back in, Handscomb punches it from the crease but finds the cover fielder.
Short in length outside off, Warner pulls it from the crease to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Walks down to the pitch of the ball and pushes it back to the bowler.

Four byes! That has gone through. Slower delivery, full and outside off, visible slow spin there as well, Warner pushes at it tamely and misses. Rahim is also foxed there and fails to collect the ball. It races behind for a boundary.
Tossed up ball on off, Handscomb comes down the track and hits it wide of mid on for a single.
Loopy full ball on off, Warner jumps out of the crease and drives it back. The bowler fails to stop it with a dive to his left and they cross for a single.
Fires one in on middle, it's defended towards mid-wicket.
Full and around off, defended solidly.

A risky shot! Skidding back into the batsman from a fuller length around off, Handscomb advances down the track and drags it over mid-wicket for a couple of runs. As a bowler, you will be happy seeing such shots being played.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Leans forward to a full ball and pushes it with the spin to covers.
Flatter and on off, stroked from the back foot to sweeper cover for a brace.

Mominul Haque drops David Warner! A costly miss. Tossed up ball on middle, spinning back in and stopping a touch on the batsman, Warner tries to flick but fails to keep it down. Mominul at short leg reacts but fails to holds onto the catch.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A good looking off drive by Handscomb after coming down the track, with the spin he plays but finds the mid off fielder. He makes a tumbling stop but cannot prevent the single.
FOUR! Good shot by Handscomb! Gets a full delivery in the middle and leg line, he gets down on one knee and sweetly times his sweep shot for a boundary at fine leg.
Slower through the air, around off and straightening a touch, Peter prods forward and defends it near his front pad.
Flatter and shorter on off, Warner taps it down in the gap at cover-point for a single.
Floated ball on middle, Warner clips it in front of square leg for a single.
Warner has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fires one in, around middle and leg, Peter paddles it fine down the leg side. The ball slows down before the fence and Sarkar retrieves it. They take three runs.
Full and on off, Handscomb has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
25th Test fifty for David Warner.
Sprays it down the leg side, Warner nudges it behind square leg for a single. Brings up his fifty. A really hard-fought one by his standards. An absolutely vital knock for his side.
Flighted and fuller on off, Warner defends it by covering the line and spin.
Uses his feet and forces it with the turn to long on for a single. Testing over!
Skidding back into the batsman, a touch on the shorter side which allows the batsman time to work it around. Handscomb helps it to square leg for one.
Straightaway Peter jumps out of the crease to smother the spin and takes it on the full. Drives it towards mid off.
Beauty of a delivery! Drifting into the batsman and landing around off, Handscomb plays for the angle but is beaten by the away spin.
Gets back and punches it down to long on for one.

Oohh...goodness me, that turned back in sharply and stayed low as well. Taijul lands it outside off, Warner decides to hang back inside the crease and eventually does well to keep it out safely. Always kept his eyes on the ball.
Presses forward and defends it watchfully to the off side. End of the over.
An arm ball around off, Handscomb draws forward to defend and gets it away from the inner half of the bat. Didn't read the variation, it seems.
Fails to land this time, a full toss on off, Handscomb hits through the line but finds mid off.
The length is too full on this occasion, not giving any chance to the ball to spin and Warner comfortably eases it down to long on for one.
Once again Warner is on the front foot to a full ball on off and blocks it with a straight bat.
Slower full ball on off, Warner leans forward and defends it back.
Shakib Al Hasan to bowl from the other end.
Uses his feet again and knocks a full ball down to long on for another run in the over.
Dances down the track to a flighted ball outside off and hits it through extra cover for a couple. Played against the spin and did well to middle it.
Warner has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flighted and outside off, Handscomb hurries down the track and drives it straight to mid off. A single taken, good active running.
Flatter and outside off, skidding away probably, Warner pushes it from the outer half of the bat to backward point for a single.
Starts with around the wicket angle to Warner, bowls it a touch short and on off, it's punched from the crease to mid off.
The players are out in the middle. Warner to take the strike with Handscomb at the other end. It shall be Taijul Islam to continue his spell. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

The pitch isn't turning square and it is looking good to bat on. However, it's getting more and more difficult out there as the sun is beaming down in Chittagong. The task for both the teams is simple. For the hosts - they need wickets and for the visitors - they need a big partnership. Australia still trail by 194 runs with 8 wickets in hand. Join us soon for the last session of the day.

A session which belongs to Australia. The pair of Smith and Warner carried on from where they left off in the last match. They stitched back-to-back fifty stands, 93 to be precise with the skipper registering yet another half century. Both were looking at ease and the bowling wasn't threatening as well. However the introduction of Taijul Islam spiced things up as he struck with his first ball to get rid of Steven Smith.
Again bowls a short ball on the stumps, Warner punches it through covers for a run. TEA ON DAY 2!
Slower through the air, on the shorter side on middle. Bounces a touch more than Warner expected. He tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
He has not got it right! Shortish ball on off, Warner camps back and pushes it through the covers for two.
Short again on middle, Handscomb pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
Drags his length back outside off, Peter punches it towards point. The fielder there fumbles but no run taken by the batsmen.
Change in bowling as Nasir Hossain comes on to bowl. Probably the last over before tea.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Drags his length back outside off, Handscomb rocks on the back foot and pushes it through covers. Nasir from mid off gives chase and saves a run for his team.
Very well bowled! Almost did Peter in length there. Tosses it up on off, turning away. Handscomb first takes a step ahead and then defends it off the back foot.
Flatter on off, Warner waits for it to turn and then flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Floats it outside off, turning back in. Warner defends it.
Slower through the air outside off, Warner pushes it to the man at covers.
Quicker on off, Warner taps it in front of covers for a run.
Loopy ball on off, Handscomb dances down and drives it towards mid off for a run.
Quicker on the stumps. Handscomb defends it solidly.
Flighted ball on off, Warner comes down the track and drives it to long off for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter on middle, Warner defends it off the front foot.
Angles it on middle and leg, turning away. Handscomb opens the face of the bat at the last moment and guides it towards point.
Shorter in length on the stumps, Handscomb defends it off the back foot.
Comes down the track but not quite to the pitch of the ball. Adjusts well and defends it.
Flighted ball on off, Peter drives it down to mid off.
Floats it up on middle, Handscomb defends it off the front foot.
Drags his length back on middle, Warner pulls it through square leg for a run.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Uses his feet and gets to the pitch of the ball. Peter flicks it to mid-wicket.
Loopy ball outside off, Warner pushes it through the off side for a run.
Flatter on the stumps, David defends it off the back foot.
Fuller on leg stump, Mehedi drives it to the fielder at mid on.
Tosses it up on off, Warner defends it solidly.
Flatter on off, Peter defends it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and around off, Peter defends it back with a forward lunge.

Very full on leg stump, turns away. Handscomb tries to work it on the leg side but gets a soft leading edge towards silly point. He lost his balance after playing it and the fielder at silly point misses his shy at the striker's end. No harm done. Replays show had he hit the stumps, even then Handscomb would have been safe.
Slower through the air on off, Peter lunges forward in defense.
Peter Handscomb comes into bat.

OUT! WOW! He does provide the breakthrough! A brilliant bowling change by the Bangladeshi skipper. Taijul bowls an arm ball on middle and off, Steven Smith plays for the turn but there isn't any. The ball goes through the gap between bat and pad and hits the stumps. A huge wicket for Bangladesh. Islam gets the big fish off his first ball. Can Bangladesh build on this now?
Taijul Islam is now into the attack. A different bowler to Shakib, bowls it a little quicker. Can he provide the breakthrough?
Darts it on off, Steven Smith guides it towards point for a run.
Loopy ball on off, Smith drives it down to wide mid off.
Fires it on off, Smith lets it turn and then works it to mid-wicket.
Quicker on middle, Warner plays it towards backward point for a run.
Shorter in length on middle, Warner pushes it off the back foot to covers.
Flatter on off, Smith goes back and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run. Too easy here for Australia. The hosts will have to try something different.
Flicks it with the angle through square leg for a run.
Loopy ball outside off, Smith drives it to covers.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
FOUR! Easy-peasy! Very slow down the leg side, very unlike Shakib. Smith shovels it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Better line and length! Tosses it up on middle, turning away. Smith defends it with authority.
Comes around the wicket now. Angles it into the pads. Smith fails to flick it and the ball hits his pads.
Flatter on off, turning in. Smith works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Floats it on off, Smith drives it to mid off.
Driven through the mid off region. They pick up a single.
21st Test fifty for Steven Smith.

Fifty for Smith! Captain leading from the front. A run machine. He keeps notching up these scores. He acknowledges the applause from his dressing room but he knows he still has a long way to go. Coming back to the ball, Smith flicks it with the spin towards square leg for a run.
Shorter in length down the leg side. Warner pulls it through short fine leg for a run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! SHOVELED! Slower through the air outside leg stump. Smith shovels it past the diving backward square leg fielder for a boundary.
Loopy ball outside leg stump, Smith pads it away.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floats it on middle, turning away. Smith defends it towards point.
Slower through the air on leg stump, Smith defends it solidly.
Flighted ball outside off, Warner waits for it and guides it down to third man for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Smith prods forward and blocks it.
Defended by getting on the front foot. All too easy at the moment for the Aussies.
Flighted ball on off, Smith defends it watchfully.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Shorter in length, turning back in. Smith tucks it to mid-wicket.
He is bowling it a touch short here. Drags his length back on the stumps. Warner works it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Gets the bottom hand in play! Flighted, full ball on the stumps. Smith drives it with the spin through covers for a couple.
Loopy ball on middle, turning away. Smith blocks it.
Comes down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Fuller on leg stump, Smith leans into it and flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Slower through the air outside leg, Smith pads it away.
Flatter outside off, no turn this time. Warner guides it towards covers for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Smith drives it back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Turns it to mid-wicket with the spin.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Works it towards mid-wicket with the angle for a run.
Flatter on off, stays a touch low. Warner does well to get his bat down in time to block it.
Flatter on leg, turning away. Smith defends it off the back foot.
Warner nails the sweep shot through square leg for a run.
Advances down the track and tries to defend it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Similar length outside off, but does not get turn. Warner manages to punch it through cover-point for a couple.

Almost chops it on! Big turn for Shakib! Bowls it slower through the air outside off, turns back in sharply. Warner first thinks about cutting it but is surprised by the turn and ends up chopping it besides short leg.
Floats it outside off, turning back in. Warner defends it off the front foot.
Loopy ball on off, Smith drives it back to the bowler.
Floats it on off, Warner eases it down to long off for a run.
Gives it air on off, David drives it to the man at covers.
Quicker on off, Warner defends it off the back foot.
Flatter on off, turning away. Warner defends it towards point.
Shorter in length on middle, Smith flicks it through square leg for a run.
FOUR! TOP SHOT! Warner sees flight and he uses his feet to get to the pitch of the ball. He drives it through covers for a boundary.
Works it with the spin to mid-wicket.
Slower through the air on off, Warner goes for the reverse sweep but misses. It takes his gloves and goes on the bounce to the man at slip.

Floats it on leg stump. Smith drives it towards mid off and sets off for a run. Tamim there is slow towards the ball but manages to score a direct hit. Anyway, the batsman has made his crease. A run added.
Bowls it outside leg. Smith pads it away.
Tosses it on leg stump, Smith works it to square leg.

Time for drinks! The heat is scorching out there. The batsmen are sitting on a chair and also have an umbrella for some shade as they are drinking water. The pair of Smith and Warner is really going along well and has also managed to keep the scoreboard ticking. Bangladesh are in need of a wicket here and will hope that one of their spinners can provide it.
Warner takes a good stride ahead and blocks it near the surface.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Quicker through the air, around off, driven back to the bowler.
Full around off, Warner presents a solid front foot defence.
Flatter and sliding into the batsman, Smith hangs back and turns it in front of square on the leg side for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full outside off, Warner covers the line of the stumps and dabs it to point.
Eased through mid off for a single.
Straying on the pads, worked to backward square leg off the back foot.

That almost sneaked through! Smith is a lucky man! Shakib bowls it quicker through the air, lands it full outside leg and the ball spins away. Smith again looks to pad it away but this time gets hit on the back pad. Luckily for him, it doesn't brush the pad and hit the woodwork behind. Shakib has his hands on his head as he knows that it was a close call. Steven needs to be more careful. Remember, he had got out in a similar fashion to Jadeja in the Ranchi Test.
Pitched outside leg, spinning towards the stumps, Smith goes back and offers no shot.
Served on the leg stump channel, Smith gets his front leg out of the way and defends it on the off side.
Tossed up outside off, David prods forward and makes a careful block.
Slides it full around off, Smith leans into the shot and eases it down to long on for a single.
Smith this time hangs back and works it in front of square on the leg side. Again finds the fielder there.
Spinning into the pads, flicked to mid-wicket.
Quicker through the air, full outside off. Warner comes forward and drives it firmly. The man at extra cover half stops it and the ball rolls towards long off. A single is taken.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full around middle, driven back to the bowler.
Warner moves across, opens the face of his bat and guides the turning in delivery square of the wicket on the off side. A single is taken.
Straighter and quicker one from Shakib. Warner kneels down to sweep but misses it completely.
Served fuller this time outside leg, Smith leans ahead and flicks it in the square leg region for a single.
A touch shorter around leg, Smith goes back and tucks it towards backward square leg.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Cover-point goes in the deep.
Quicker through the air, pitched full around off, Warner prods ahead and blocks it.
Served around off, Smith leans ahead to defend. He plays for the turn but it isn't there. The ball then takes the outside edge and rolls in the backward point region for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Spinning into the pads, nudged behind square on the leg side for a brace.
Served around middle and off, spinning in, tapped back to the bowler.
50-run stand is up between Warner and Smith!
Sliding into the pads, Warner goes back and works it through wide mid on. They pick up a single and bring up their consecutive 50-run stand as well.
Mehedi Hasan is back into the attack!
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full outside off, pushed to mid off.
Flatter delivery, sliding into the pads, worked off the back foot in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Wide outside off, spinning in, Warner shuffles across, then backs away and cuts it in the point region for a single.

Once again Shakib tosses it up nicely, lands it outside off and gets it to turn a long way in. Warner once again gets a good stride forward to defend but misses and the ball lobs off the pads on the leg side.

Shout for a catch! Beautifully bowled by Shakib. He tosses it up nicely outside off, Warner prods a long way forward to defend but the ball sneaks through and the ball lobs off something to Sarkar at first slip. The players appeal but the umpire stays put.
Fullish outside off, Smith prods forward and blocks it on the off side.
Angling into the batsman, defended down the track.
Pitched fuller outside off, Smith leans ahead and defends.

FOUR! Delightful! A boundary to bring up 50 for Australia! Full and wide outside off, Smith frees his arms and drives it with perfect timing. Gets it through point and away to the fence. The Aussie skipper has punished almost every delivery landed in that area.
Full and angling into the batsman, pushed to mid on with a straight bat.
Full on middle, Smith covers the stumps and flicks it straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Warner lets it spin into him and works it to mid-wicket.

Very, very slow through the air on off, turning away but slow turn. Smith has all the time in the world. He rocks onto the back foot and cuts it towards point. The fielder misfields and concedes a single.
Flatter outside off, Warner guides it through point for a run.
Comes down the track. Shakib sees him and drags his length back. Warner adjusts and defends it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Works it with the turn towards wide mid on.
Shakib Al Hasan is introduced into the attack.
Just ahead of a length on off, Smith defends it solidly.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Overcompensating here, Rahman. Bowls it on the pads this time. Smith flicks it through backward square leg for a brace.
FOUR! STREAKY! Rahman bowls it full and wide outside off. Smith goes for a very lazy drive and gets an edge through the vacant second slip region for a boundary.
Comes around the wicket and angles it on the pads. Smith flicks it to mid-wicket.
Fuller in length on the stumps. Trying to get Smith LBW. Steven does well to keep it out.

Low full toss on leg stump, Warner drives it back past the diving bowler but straight to mid on. Warner wanted a run and he takes a few steps ahead but is sent back by Smith. The fielder there fumbles and there is no harm done. Had he collected it cleanly it would have been interesting.
Drags his length back on middle, Smith punches it to long on for a run.
A similar delivery and a similar shot to the way he got out in the first Test. Fuller in length on middle, Smith plants his front foot forward and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Serves a gift, a full toss on the stumps. Smith drives it straight to mid off. He should have put that away.
Fires it on the pads, Smith works it to short mid-wicket.
Works it past the diving short fine leg fielder for a couple.
Angles it into the pads, Warner flicks it through square leg for a brace.
Good length on middle, Warner defends it off the front foot.

FOUR! This time Rahman gets the edge but it flies through the slip cordon for a boundary. Shorter in length outside off, Warner tries to force it through the off side but gets an outside edge to the third man fence.
Almost an edge! A little short outside off. Warner seeing the width on offer tries to cut but gets beaten.
Lands it on a length on middle, David defends it off the back foot.
Rahman comes steaming in and bowls a full delivery on middle, Warner pushes it back to him.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
FOUR! EASY! Fuller this time outside off, Smith drives it through cover-point for a boundary.
FOUR! Poor line and length! Shorter and down the leg side. Smith flicks it through short fine leg for a boundary.

Fuller on leg stump, Warner flicks it towards mid on and sets off for a run. The fielder there picks the ball up and has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. A run added. These two are lightning quick between the wickets.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Slower through the air on leg stump, straightens a touch. Warner tries to work it on the leg side but gets a soft leading edge towards mid off.
Back of a length on off, Warner punches it through point for a run.
Flicks it with the angle to mid-wicket.
Sprays it on the pads, Smith misses the flick as the ball brushes the pads and goes down to fine leg. The batsmen take a leg bye.

That was just a punch and it almost went to the fence. A touch fuller in length around off, Warner punches it through covers. The fielder, Shakib from mid off gives it a chase and does well to pull the ball back in. Taijul does the mopping up job. The batsmen run three.
Bowls it on the pads, Steven flicks it through square leg for a run.
Fuller in length on middle, Smith eases it to mid on.
Mustafizur will bowl from the other end. He already has a wicket to his name. Bangladesh would want him to get one of these two out.
Flights it on a length on off, turns a touch away from the batsman. Warner adjusts well and guides it towards point.
Angles it into the pads, Warner flicks it to short fine leg.
Quicker on middle, Warner defends it solidly.
Floats it on off, Warner pushes it past the diving cover fielder and towards deep mid off. He wanted a run but then opts against it.
Shorter in length outside off, David cuts it to point.
Starts off with a flatter delivery on middle, does not spin, goes on with the arm. Warner lunges forward and keeps it out.

We're ready to get underway. The men concerned are out in the middle. David Warner (wearing a cap) and Steven Smith will resume their innings. Mehedi Hasan will continue his spell. He has a slip and a short leg in place. Here we go....
...Day 2, Session 2...

A little passage before lunch and Bangladesh will be buoyed after picking the wicket of Matt Renshaw. Australia will be feeling the early heat but they have two of their most senior batsmen in the middle and all their hopes will be pinned on these two. Expect a lot of spin test for them post lunch. Do join us in a short while.
Back of a length on off, Smith stays back and keeps it out. LUNCH ON DAY 2!
Fullish in length on off, Smith drives it to mid off.
FOUR! He is so good through the off side! Fuller and width on offer outside off, Smith's eyes lit up there. He leans into it and drives it through point for a boundary.
Good length on off, angling away from the batsman. Smith defends it towards point.
Lands it on a length around off, Smith defends it off the back foot.
Fuller in length around off, Smith eases it to mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fires it on the pads, Smith tries to flick and misses. The ball brushes the pads as it goes towards fine leg. The players appeal but the umpire remains put. The batsmen take a leg bye.
Plays it with the turn on the leg side.
Works it around the corner with the angle for a run. That went really close to the short leg fielder. There were shouts of 'CATCH IT' but he just could not react that fast.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Fires it down the leg side, Smith goes for the flick but misses.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! What a shot to get off the mark! Rahman serves a half volley outside off. Smith leans into it and caresses it through covers for a boundary.
Steven Smith is the next man in.

OUT! Captain fantastic. Mushfiqur Rahim takes an absolute blinder! Rahman draws first blood but a lot of credit has to be given to the keeper. Mustafizur bowls it down the leg side, Renshaw goes for the flick but gets a thick inside edge to the right of the keeper. Rahim dives full stretch and takes it with one hand. An early wicket for Bangladesh and they are ecstatic. The crowd erupts as well. This is also the first time a Bangladeshi pacer has taken a wicket in this series.
Lands it on a length on middle, Warner tries to defend but gets an inside edge through square leg for a run.
Fuller in length on middle, Warner drives it to mid on.
Spin from one end and seam from the other. Mustafizur Rahman will bowl from the other end.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Quicker on off, comes in with the angle. The batsman defends it solidly.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! LOVELY SHOT! Mehedi tosses it up on middle, Renshaw leans into it and drives it through mid on for a boundary. Australia are underway.
Bowls it on the stumps, Renshaw defends it watchfully.

Starts off with a flatter ball outside off, turning away from the batsman. Renshaw leaves it but then raises his hands up in anger. He might have some issue with the sightscreen. There might be somebody passing from there as the ball was being bowled. It would have been interesting to see what would have happened had the ball been on the stumps.
